name: read-connectors-derived-crossing-ends
description: A computed value on request: `derived: ["crossing_ends"]` at the `connectors` layer adds to each connector the end pairs that cross a partition — for each provider/requester pair `connection_ends` gives, one value per combination of a provider partition and a requester partition (each end's component's `partitions`) that differ, as `connection_ends`' value with `"partition"` added to each end. Composed from the two owned answers, never a second formula. Set-valued (`rows: "one per value"`): a connector that crosses no partition has no row, so the answer is exactly the crossing set; an end whose component no partition runs crosses nothing here.

context.summary: The seed of `read-swc-derived-partitions`: `ExampleSWC` runs in `PARTITION1` on `CORE1` and `ExampleConsumerSWC` in `PARTITION0` on `CORE0`, so the base's one connector, `Example_to_Consumer`, crosses from `PARTITION1` to `PARTITION0`.
context.notes: A read takes no scope and writes no audit record.

expected.notes: The protocol has no comparison operator between two values of a row, so without `crossing_ends` the question "which connections cross a partition" would read every connector and every component's partitions and compare them on the client. `crossing_ends` applies at the elements of the `connectors` layer alone: asked elsewhere it is `schema-violation`, never a blank.
